Title: Explosions heard in Saudi capital as airport due to reopen
Article:
Explosions heard in Saudi capital as airport due to reopen
AFP
RIYADH: Explosions rang out in the Saudi capital on Sunday, as the kingdom was due to reopen Riyadh international airport despite repeated attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
Saudi Arabia, which leads a military coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthis, has faced a barrage of strikes from the group in recent weeks.
The fighting erupted after a years-long truce between the Houthis and Yemen's Riyadh-backed government fell apart.
Riyadh's international airport said flights would resume on Sunday after a two-week closure following the Houthi strikes.
However it remained unclear to what extent the airport was operational.
The Houthi fighters have carried out waves of strikes on the airport, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
The group has also targeted oil infrastructure and other sites, with the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen announcing on Sunday it had intercepted 10 Houthi missiles fired at southern Saudi Arabia.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that Riyadh airport was still "unsafe" and a "military target."
"The Yemeni Armed Forces warn all international, regional and local airlines – as well as staff and travellers – against using King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, as it is unsafe and serves as a military target for our forces," he said.
"The Saudi regime shall bear the consequences of any operations at the airport."
- Attack warning -
An AFP journalist in the city heard three explosions in the early hours of Sunday, with residents receiving alert messages for a "hostile aerial threat" urging them to stay in a safe place.
The warning came as the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had downed a ballistic missile launched by the group towards Riyadh, as well as two drones in the capital area.
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh," the coalition posted on X.
Later Sunday morning, the coalition said its forces intercepted a cruise missile fired by the Houthis at the kingdom's southern city of Khamis Mushait.
Attacks appeared to target areas across the south, with warnings also issued for Abha city and Namas Governorate.
"The bombardment has been very heavy since this morning – may God keep us safe. Everything is shaking because of the explosions," one resident in Khamis Mushait told AFP Sunday on condition of anonymity.
The attacks came after the Houthi fighters said that – in the space of 24 hours – they targeted three Saudi airports, including in Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base.
The Saudi civil defence agency said it had also responded to falling debris in the Mecca and Medina regions on Saturday after intercepting two Houthi missiles.
The Houthis denied targeting the cities, the two holiest in Islam, calling the Saudi claim a "huge lie."
The Houthis also fired at the southern Yemeni city of Aden, the interim seat of the Saudi-backed government, saying they targeted a naval base and military camp overseen by Saudi forces.
The flare-up in Yemen, with the Houthis taking control of the entire Red Sea coast in a lightning offensive last month, has further destabilised the region and disrupted oil markets.
The Houthi attacks have dealt a blow to Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest exporter of crude, disrupting businesses, airlines and residents, and rattling its drive to shift its international image.

Title: PN chairman: Does Bersatu still have its heart in PN?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar has questioned whether Bersatu is still committed to the coalition, citing developments since the Negri Sembilan state election.
He said Bersatu had been invited to tonight's emergency PN supreme council meeting and that it was up to the party to attend.
"With what has happened lately, since the Negri Sembilan election, does Bersatu still its heart in Perikatan Nasional?"
"But as far as the meeting goes, it can go ahead. They can come. We said we invited Bersatu to come to the meeting. It's up to them," he told reporters before the meeting at Pas headquarters here.

Title: Bersatu not the court, emergency PN meeting is compulsory for all parties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional information chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa has criticised Bersatu for questioning the legality of tonight's emergency supreme council meeting, saying the party cannot take over the role of the court.
He said the meeting was compulsory as the coalition needed to discuss its preparations for the Melaka election.
"That's the problem. If we don't call them, they say they weren't called. When they are called, they come up with all sorts of excuses.
"The Bersatu secretary-general (Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali) cannot take over the court's role. And Bersatu is not the court. We uphold the rule of law.
"The court has made its decision. And we are allowed to contest and use the logo, which means we can carry out activities until the court says otherwise," he told reporters before the emergency PN meeting at Pas headquarters here.
He said the meeting had two main items on the agenda, namely feedback on the court order and the Melaka election.
"We are facing the Melaka election, so how can we not hold a meeting? If we don't hold a meeting, Bersatu will be the one to complain.
"We must also announce our candidates. And before announcing candidates, there must be discussions among the component parties," he said, adding that Barisan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan had already announced theirs.
"So the meeting is compulsory. If the court says we can, then we must meet. Stop making excuses."
Annuar also questioned Bersatu's commitment to the coalition.
"I think what Bersatu is doing, shame on them. It will come back on them and people will ask what their real intention is. Is Bersatu still prepared to be with Perikatan Nasional? Or do they actually want to see Perikatan Nasional destroyed?"
Annuar said disloyalty by any party was a "very serious breach" under the constitution.
"We know Bersatu has breached discipline many times, including contesting against its own party's candidates. So, I think enough is enough. Let's move on and take part in the Melaka election together," he said.
He said Bersatu should attend the meeting even if it believed the gathering could not be held.
"Come. Sit down and have some coffee first. We have six parties, they need to hear from the other five.
"They will put out a press statement, right? They don't dare to come," he said.
Earlier, Azmin had warned that the meeting could carry
serious legal implications
as the coalition's registration had been cancelled.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan had said on Oct 22 that the coalition would
invite Bersatu
to an upcoming meeting after the High Court granted a stay against the Registrar of Societies' action.

Title: Syed Saddiq, Bella's kenduri rakyat swarmed by people since morning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Even before the event began, crowds had already started streaming into the venue of the kenduri rakyat hosted by Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and his new wife, singer and actress Bella Astillah.
Some had been queuing for hours from early morning to ensure they could attend the event, held at the Yong Sheng Banquet Hall in Jalan Bakri, Muar, today.
In a post on Threads, a user known as Taufiq Ridzuan shared a video showing people queuing as early as 8am, despite the event being scheduled to begin only at 2pm.
The post reflected the public's excitement in joining in the celebration, with the couple having taken a different approach by hosting an open wedding feast for the community.
Syed Saddiq had earlier explained that the concept of the wedding feast was intended to bring their celebration closer to the people, while reviving the tradition of rewang, a communal practice deeply rooted in Malay culture where members of the community come together to help prepare for celebrations.
Adding to the significance of the occasion, besides food and drinks being served to guests, essential household items were distributed as tokens of appreciation to those who attended.
The event received support from sponsors, with contributions worth more than RM500,000 in the form of food, drinks, rice, coconut milk and essential goods, besides laptops, to be distributed during the celebration.
Syed Saddiq and Bella were officially married on Oct 10 in a solemnisation ceremony held at Level 118 of Menara Merdeka 118 here.
The couple held a wedding reception at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) on Oct 18.
On Saturday, the couple will hold another kenduri rakyat, this time in Sabah, where Bella was born.

Title: Crocodile caught in fisherman's net in Sabah
Article:
KOTA MARUDU: A fisherman was surprised to find a crocodile caught in his fishing net near Kampung Radu Laut Pangkalan.
The man contacted the Fire and Rescue Department for assistance after discovering the crocodile at about 8.45am.
Kota Marudu Fire and Rescue Station chief Debli Mamoi said: "Upon arrival, the fire and rescue team found a 2m-long crocodile caught in the fishing net," he said.
Recently, a 2.8m-long, 100kg crocodile was also found trapped in a fishing net at Kampung Birahan.
The fire and rescue department advised the public, particularly fishermen, to remain alert to the presence of crocodiles in the waters and contact the authorities immediately if they spot one.

Title: Fahmi: 2 journalists involved in road accident to get Tabung Kasih@HAWANA aid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two journalists involved in a road accident in Perak this morning will receive assistance under the Tabung Kasih@HAWANA initiative, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said the Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), was arranging assistance for Bernama journalist Nur Afiradina Arshad and New Straits Times (NST) journalist Zahratulhayat Md Arif.
"I was just informed by Bernama editor-in-chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj that both journalists involved in the accident in Menglembu, along Jalan Ipoh-Lumut, this morning had received treatment at Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital in Ipoh and did not sustain any serious injuries.
"I pray that everything goes smoothly for both of them and that they make a full recovery," he said in a Facebook post.
Nur Afiradina, 34, and Zahratulhayat, 37, were travelling to Bagan Datuk to cover an event involving Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi when a lorry hit the rear of their Perodua Bezza at traffic lights at about 6am.
Tabung Kasih@HAWANA is a welfare initiative established in conjunction with National Journalists' Day (Hawana) to assist journalists, former media practitioners and veteran journalists facing health problems, personal hardships or financial difficulties.
The initiative is managed by Bernama on behalf of the Communications Ministry to strengthen the social safety net for media practitioners nationwide. -- BERNAMA

Title: Landslide buries two cars near Tanjung Tokong condo
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A landslide near Leisure Bay Condominium in Tanjung Tokong this evening partially buried two cars, with no casualties reported.
The Penang Fire and Rescue Department received a distress call at 6.50pm.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the landslide buried a BMW and a Honda City, both parked nearby.
"No casualties were reported," he said.
John said six personnel were deployed to the scene with the police also assisting in the operation, which is still ongoing.
Further information will be updated as the operation progresses.

Title: Melaka election: Amanah satisfied with five seats, to focus on winning all
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Amanah vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad says the party is grateful to be contesting five seats in the Melaka election on Nov 14.
He said Pakatan Harapan remains united on the seat allocation, adding that Amanah, which has been part of PH since the coalition's formation in 2015, had always acted in tandem with its partners.
"What matters most in any election is that Amanah has consistently acted — forgive me if this sounds 'holier-than-thou' as that is not my intention — in tandem as a unified coalition.
"You rarely hear of internal conflicts within Pakatan Harapan during elections," he told reporters after the 2026 National Mental Health Month Celebration today.
Dzulkefly said the allocation was finalised after exhaustive deliberations and negotiations, and all levels of the coalition would abide by the decision of PH's top leadership.
He said Amanah would now focus on winning all five seats.
"Being allocated many seats is meaningless if you don't win them. What we have is sufficient, and we will do our utmost to support one another and deliver victories for all Pakatan Harapan candidates contesting in Melaka," he said.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced 21 PH candidates for the 28-seat Melaka polls, with Amanah Melaka chairman Adly Zahari set to
defend his Bukit Katil seat
.

Title: Amanah accepts 5 seats for Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) has accepted Pakatan Harapan's (PH) seat allocation for the Melaka  election, despite being allocated five seats compared with nine in the 2021 election.
Its vice-president, Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, said the decision followed thorough negotiations at the coalition's highest level.
"What matters to Amanah in any election is that we have been part of PH since its formation in 2015. We have always acted, organised and carried out our campaigns as a united coalition.
"The decision by PH's top leadership was made after thorough discussions and negotiations," he said after officiating at the 2026 National Mental Health Month celebration here today.
Dzulkefly, who is also Health Minister, said all party machinery, from top leaders and middle management to the grassroots, would comply with the coalition committee's decision.
"We are grateful to have been allocated five seats, and we hope to win all of them.
"There is no benefit in being allocated many seats if we fail to win them.
"Therefore, we will do our best to support one another to ensure all PH partner candidates contesting the election win," he said.
Under the seat allocation for the Melaka election on Nov 14, PKR will contest nine state seats, DAP seven and Amanah five, bringing the coalition's total to 21 seats.

Title: Workplace mental health policy in final stages, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry is finalising a workplace mental health policy.
This is after more than 55,000 civil servants were found to be at high risk of mental health issues, including suicidal tendencies.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said engagement sessions with stakeholders were ongoing, and an official announcement would be made once the policy was finalised.
"We are still in the process of broader stakeholder consultations. We want to avoid creating a policy in silo, or developed without sufficient cross-agency input," he told reporters after the 2026 National Mental Health Month Celebration today.
In his speech earlier, Dzulkefly cited a Public Service Department report based on its MyPsyD screening system, which found more than 55,000 civil servants to be at high risk of mental health issues, including suicidal tendencies.
"These findings serve as a timely reminder that the workplace is not merely a platform for pursuing key performance indicators (KPIs) and productivity," he said.
He said depression among adults had doubled from 500,000 in 2019 to one million in 2023, according to the 2023 National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS).
"We are also witnessing emotional distress and suicidal behaviour taking a toll on our younger generation," he said.
He added that more engagements were required to complete the mental health policy draft, and an official announcement would be made once it has been finalised.
In July, Dzulkefly had said
the engagement sessions
would involve the Human Resources Ministry, Occupational Safety and Health Department, Malaysian Employers Federation and Malaysian Trades Union Congress.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang Sultan, Tengku Ampuan extend condolences on passing of Kelantan Sultan's aunt
Article:
KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, has conveyed his condolences to the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V, and the Kelantan royal family, following the death of Datuk Tengku Rozan Almarhum Sultan Yahya Petra yesterday.
The Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, also extended her condolences on the passing of the Kelantan Sultan's aunt.
According to a Pahang Sultanate Facebook post, Their Royal Highnesses expressed their sorrow over her passing and hoped that the entire Kelantan royal family would be granted fortitude and strength in facing this difficult time of grief.
"May Allah shower His mercy upon the deceased's soul, forgive all her sins and place her among the faithful and righteous," Their Royal Highnesses said.
Tengku Rozan died at 9.10pm yesterday.

Title: Haze: 8 areas record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eight areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 6pm today, with Serian police headquarters in Sarawak recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 192.
According to the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five other monitoring stations in Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings, namely Kuching (180), Samarahan (177), Sri Aman (157), Sibu (152) and Sarikei (109).
Unhealthy API readings were also recorded in Terengganu, with Paka registering 156, while Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded 152.
Meanwhile, APIMS reported that 50 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 10 areas remained at the good level.
API readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are classified as hazardous.

Title: Gunung Jerai villages hit by floods repeatedly
Article:
YAN: Residents of Kampung Titi Teras and Kampung Teroi Bukit at the foot of Gunung Jerai are facing floods again after five hours of continuous heavy rain caused a river to overflow into their homes early today.
Kampung Titi Teras Village Community Council chairman Kamarudin Arifin said initial checks found about 20 houses affected by the floods.
He said residents grew worried and prepared for possible flooding whenever heavy rain continued.
"Since the beginning of the year, the area has been flooded more than five times, with the latest incident on Sept 20.
"Some residents have moved out, while others have remained in their homes. I hope they will be prepared if the weather gets worse," he said when met here today.
Kampung Titi Teras resident Sharip Saod, 75, said heavy rain that began at about 10pm yesterday caused water levels to rise at around 3am.
He said he, his wife and their son, who is in his 40s, stayed awake to monitor the water level and ensure their family's safety.
"We have been awake since last night because the rain has not stopped. So far, things are still under control. We have moved whatever household belongings we could save to the side.
"It is exhausting to be hit by floods so often, but there is nothing we can do except face it," he said.
Yan Civil Defence Force officer Lieutenant (PA) Muhammad Zul Izzi Zulkifli advised residents, particularly the elderly and other vulnerable groups, to evacuate if instructed by the authorities.
Monitoring showed that water levels had yet to change significantly and could rise further due to the high tide, delaying the recession of floodwaters, he said.
He said the Malaysian Meteorological Department had also forecast continuous rain in the area over the next few days.
The latest data showed that 105 flood victims in two districts had been affected. Of these, 65 were housed at the SK Teroi temporary relief centre in Yan, while another 40 were at the Surau As Saadiah relief centre in Gurun, Kuala Muda.

Title: GPS needs to continue leading Sarawak to sustain development, says deputy premier
Article:
KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) must continue to lead the state government to ensure the continuity of socioeconomic development and to keep the future of the people on the right track, said Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Awang Tengah Ali Hasan.
He urged the people of Sarawak to support GPS in the 13th state election, noting that the current administration has demonstrated a clear direction in driving inclusive progress that encompasses both urban and rural areas.
"That is why we have no other choice. Our choice is the existing government led by the Premier of Sarawak (Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg), the GPS government which has a clear vision to implement transformation and elevate the well-being of the people.
"We (GPS) have an inclusive policy, we develop Sarawak through the cooperation of all races within the state," he said while speaking at the launching of Anjung Usahawan (Entrepreneurs' Hub) and the Sematan Industrial Park in Lundu.
Awang Tengah, who is also the Bukit Sari assemblyman, gave his assurance that GPS remains committed to strengthening the state's development agenda for the benefit of the people and future generations.
Regarding the polling date for the state election, he said the matter falls entirely under the jurisdiction of the Election Commission (EC).
"But one thing is certain,  we must work together and work hard, we cannot take anything for granted. It is a matter of our collective strength and our future standing.
"We want to bequeath to our children and grandchildren a Sarawak that is more prosperous and united," he said.
Last Friday, during a special press conference, Abang Johari announced the
dissolution
of the Sarawak state legislative assembly, effective tomorrow, to pave the way for the 13th state election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: One psychiatrist per 69,000 people in Malaysia as govt targets improved ratio
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry aims to have one psychiatrist for every 40,000 people, compared with the current ratio of one for every 69,000.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the target, aimed at meeting growing demand for mental health services, would be achieved by expanding specialist training.
He said the ministry employed about 400 of the country's roughly 700 registered psychiatrists, with the rest working in the private sector.
"This highlights the urgent need to expand our psychiatric workforce to match this escalating demand.
"Having sufficient psychiatrists to meet growing demand is undeniably a major challenge.
"Human resource constraints are a legacy issue I inherited, but we are doing everything we can," he told reporters today at the 2026 National Mental Health Month Celebration.
To ease the shortage, Dzulkefly said the ministry was also adopting 'task-shifting', whereby counsellors and family medicine specialists (FMS) take on part of the mental health caseload.
"This enables us to ease the workload and meet staffing needs effectively, rather than relying solely on psychiatrists," he said.
He said there were 10,000 registered counsellors nationwide, of whom 300 worked with the ministry.
He added that mental health services were offered at 1,116 government clinics, while psychiatric services were available at 68 ministry hospitals and four psychiatric institutions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, UAE discuss Middle East situation, UN secretary-general nomination
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) exchanged views on current global developments, particularly the ongoing situation in the Middle East, according to a post by Malaysia's Foreign Ministry on the social media platform X on Sunday.
The ministry said the discussion took place on Friday during a telephone conversation between Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Affairs Minister His Highness Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
The ongoing situation in Middle East remains a primary focus of the international community, the posting added.
The ministry also said Mohamad had extended his heartfelt congratulations to the UAE on the nomination of Lana Nusseibeh as a candidate for the position of United Nations (UN) secretary-general.
Turkiye's national news agency, Anadolu Ajansi, recently reported that Nusseibeh, the UAE's Minister of State and envoy to the UN and the European Union (EU), had announced her candidacy following her formal nomination by the UAE.
Current UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres is due to complete his second term on Dec 31.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CGS International keeps "Add" call on My DIY
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mr DIY Group (M) Bhd's exposure to rising e-commerce competition such as China's Pinduoduo free shipping campaign is among the reasons that the stock has been underperforming, according to CGS International.
The firm also attributed the slowdown to lower foreign shareholding following its reclassification to the MSCI Malaysia Small Cap Index in May.
"While the market views Mr DIY as highly exposed to rising e-commerce competition, we believe Pinduoduo's appeal is largely confined to price-sensitive purchases where immediate product availability is less important," it said in a note.
Mr DIY's stock has dropped 24.84 per cent on a year-to-date basis and 33.14 per cent over the past 12 months.
CGS International said that Pinduoduo's free shipping is a short-term marketing subsidy funded by PDD Holdings, similar to its strategy in the US and Europe.
It estimated Pinduoduo's Malaysia e-commerce market share at between RM1 billion and RM3 billion per annum or 1.4 to 3.4 per cent, less than 0.4 per cent of Malaysia's total retail sales.
As Pinduoduo does not disclose country-level gross merchandise value, the firm derived its estimates using four public data points.
Given that Pinduoduo's Malaysian push only gained traction in between March and April 2026, it is assumed that Pinduoduo's taxable low-value goods imports will grow in a similar trend as last year and the platform captures between 20 per cent and 50 per cent of the RM5.8 billion increase, implying a gross merchandise value of between RM1.2 billion and RM2.89 billion for 2026.
"Based on our assumptions, Pinduoduo likely loses between RM1.53 and RM8.22 per item shipped to Malaysia and would require an average item value of between RM49 and RM163 to break even under our low- and base-case scenarios," it said in a note.
The firm noted that Mr DIY's second-quarter operations overlapped with Pinduoduo's viral period between March and April this year but Mr DIY's transactions rose 7.3 per cent year-on-year, with gross margin held at 47.4 per cent.
"In our view, stabilising transactions per store and basket value after the price lock expiry would ease investor concerns over Pinduoduo."
The firm added that the Malaysian government's potential introduction of the E-Commerce Bill in the next parliamentary session could benefit Mr DIY and other value retailers.
CGS International cut its core net profit forecasts for Mr DIY by 8.2 per cent in the financial years 2027 (FY27) and FY28. It expects Pinduoduo's free shipping campaign to weigh on transactions and basket size in the first half of 2027 (1H27), before the proposed E-Commerce Bill takes effect in 2H27.
This reduces its FY27 and FY28 revenue forecasts by 2.6 per cent each as the firm assumes no catch-up in lost sales once free shipping normalises.
CGS International kept its "Add" call on the stock with a lower target price of RM1.90.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man found dead near food stall in Cheras [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man in his mid-20s was found unconscious and later pronounced dead near a food stall at Flat Sri Melaka, Jalan Ikan Emas, Cheras.
Cheras district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said police received a report about the discovery at 9.02am.
Investigating officers, members of the Salak Selatan police station's Criminal Investigation Division and the police forensic team were deployed to the scene.
View on Threads
The man was pronounced dead at the scene, Mohd Rosdi said.
Initial checks found no foul play.
The body has been sent to the forensic unit at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz in Cheras. The case has been classified as sudden death.
Earlier, photographs and videos showing a man lying outside a food stall at Flat Sri Melaka went viral on Threads.

Title: One in 23 Malaysian women now at risk of breast cancer
Article:
KUCHING: The risk of Malaysian women developing breast cancer has risen to one in 23, compared with one in 27 previously, says Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said that based on the Malaysian National Cancer Registry Report for 2012–2016 and 2017–2021, breast cancer remains the most common cancer among women in the country.
"More concerning, the National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2023 found that 71 per cent of women aged 40 and above have never undergone a mammogram, while 46 per cent do not practise breast self-examination.
"This low screening rate complicates early detection efforts, even though the survival rate for patients detected at an early stage can reach 95 per cent," she said at the Sarawak state-level Breast Cancer Awareness Month event today.
Nancy said that to widen access to early breast cancer screening, the government, through the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), has introduced the Mammogram Examination Subsidy Programme since 2007.
She said the programme was later strengthened and rebranded to WeCaRe, which encompasses awareness of breast and cervical cancer among women.
As of Sept 30, she said, 598,919 women in Malaysia have benefited from the programme, including 90,075 women in Sarawak, with 88 of them testing positive for cancer.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Johor schools to reopen in phases, exam candidates first
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Schools in Johor will reopen in phases, with the first phase on tomorrow and Tuesday limited to students sitting for examinations according to the scheduled timetable.
State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made following the decree of the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, who places great importance on the safety, health and well-being of the people of Johor.
He said the arrangement would also give school administrators and teachers time to prepare for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Ujian Akhir Sesi Akademik (UASA) examinations.
"The second phase will begin on Wednesday, when all schools throughout Johor are scheduled to resume full operations as usual, subject to developments in air quality," he said in a statement.
Naqib said the Johor Education Department would coordinate the implementation of health and safety standard operating procedures (SOPs), including the wearing of face masks and monitoring of school activities, based on current air pollutant index (API) readings.
He said the state government and relevant agencies would continue to monitor the haze situation closely to ensure that any necessary action could be taken based on assessments of prevailing conditions.
Yesterday, the Johor government decided that all educational institutions would resume operations tomorrow after taking into account developments in the haze situation and assessments by the relevant agencies.
As of 4pm today, only two districts in Johor recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Pasir Gudang at 154 and Batu Pahat at 127.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No piranha found or caught in Klau dam in Raub - Fisheries dept
Article:
KUANTAN: No piranha fish were found or caught during the Alien Fish Mitigation Programme at the Klau Dam, Raub, which took place over two days starting yesterday, said Fisheries director-general Datuk Adnan Hussain.
However, this situation cannot be interpreted as proof that the species is no longer present in the dam, following previous reports confirming the discovery of piranhas in the area.
He said this mitigation program is one of the inland fisheries management efforts to control alien fish populations and reduce the risk of disruption to native fish species.
"No piranha fish were found or caught throughout this program. However, monitoring and scientific assessment must continue to identify the presence and distribution of the species," he said via a media statement today.
Previously, a video went viral on social media regarding the discovery of a fish allegedly resembling a
piranha
at the Klau Dam, Raub, sparking various reactions from the public.
The Fisheries Department added in the same release that, apart from catching activities, research using the environmental DNA (eDNA) method was also carried out during this programme to help detect the possible presence of piranhas in the Klau Dam.
This method allows water samples to be analysed to detect genetic material that may have been left behind by aquatic organisms.
"The final results of the eDNA research will be determined after the analysis and scientific evaluation process is completed. Therefore, any conclusion regarding the status of piranha presence in the Klau Dam must take into account these analysis results alongside relevant monitoring information and field evidence," according to the statement.
The department said that this programme also aims to reduce the alien fish population, assess the fish composition in the dam's waters, and increase public awareness of the threat posed by alien species to aquatic biodiversity and ecosystem balance.
The programme, conducted at the approximately 25sqkm dam, involved 150 participants, consisting of 100 anglers, 32 cast-net participants, and 18 gill-net participants.
"Throughout the programme, a total of 156.6kg of alien fish were recorded, involving three main groups, namely Peacock Bass, Zebra Tilapia, and Javanese Carp (Lampam Jawa)," according to the statement.

Title: [UPDATED] Bersatu warns of legal risks over PN emergency meeting
Article:
\KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu has warned that today's emergency Perikatan Nasional (PN) Supreme Council meeting could carry serious legal implications as the coalition's registration has been cancelled.
Bersatu secretary-general, Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, said all parties should preserve the status quo of the Registrar of Societies' decision until all court proceedings had been exhausted.
He questioned why Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan had issued the invitation to the meeting on Oct 23 when a notice of appeal had been filed at the Court of Appeal on the same day on behalf of the Registrar of Societies and the Home Minister.
"If Pas and its allies still proceed with the 'Perikatan Nasional Supreme Council' meeting in the situation explained above, Bersatu is concerned that the proceedings of the meeting and the decisions made at it carry serious legal implications," he said in a statement today.
He said that although PN obtained a stay from the High Court on Oct 22, the court had noted that the deregistration had already taken effect.
"The court also accepted that a stay order cannot be automatically deemed to restore a registration that has been cancelled," he said.
He said that under the Societies Act 1966, a deregistered society becomes unlawful, while any office-bearer or person managing it commits an offence punishable by up to five years in jail.
"Bersatu will bring this matter to be discussed with lawyers to ensure that the implementation of the law in accordance with the PN Constitution and the Societies Act 1966 is carried out lawfully and in an orderly manner," he said.
He added that the meeting's organisers must first state their position on the Bersatu Supreme Leadership Council quorum issue and Bersatu's membership in PN. He said these issues had been used to deny the party's right to attend and vote at the coalition's Supreme Council meeting on July 16.
"They also often dispute Bersatu's membership when Bersatu is a legitimate member party of PN, as affirmed by the Registrar of Societies in a letter dated Aug 12, 2026," he said.
On Oct 13, the High Court granted PN leave to initiate a
judicial review against two actions
by the Registrar of Societies: a show-cause notice under Section 13(2) of the Societies Act 1966 and an order under Section 13(2)(A) suspending the coalition's activities.
The Registrar of Societies confirmed on Oct 20 that it had
cancelled PN's registration,
saying the coalition's explanation had failed to address the grounds for cancellation outlined in an earlier notice.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cops nab 6 over restaurant brawl in Lahad Datu
Article:
LAHAD DATU: Six people, including three women, have been arrested over a fight at a restaurant here believed to have been sparked by jealousy.
The suspects, aged between 19 and 38, were arrested at 8pm yesterday.
Lahad Datu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Dzulbaharin Ismail said preliminary investigations indicated that the fight stemmed from jealousy.
"The misunderstanding is believed to have also involved a female worker's boyfriend and several other individuals," he said in a statement today.
Dzulbaharin said the case was being investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting.
Earlier, a video lasting about 30 seconds circulated on social media showing a man being chased by a group of people before falling and being beaten outside a restaurant.

Title: PH-Bersatu cooperation could widen Malay voter reach in Melaka election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cooperation with Bersatu could help Pakatan Harapan (PH) reach more Malay voters in next month's Melaka election, but wresting power from Barisan Nasional (BN) will remain difficult.
Universiti Malaya senior political science lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said PH would need to win 15 of the 28 seats contested, but several factors favoured BN.
These included the performance of Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, BN's "poster boy", the performance of several BN assemblymen, and Umno-BN's popularity and grassroots strength in Melaka.
Mohammad Tawfik said DAP's four seats in Kota Laksamana, Kesidang, Bandar Hilir and Ayer Keroh would be difficult to challenge, as each had previously been won with a majority of more than 5,000 votes.
"However, it is still too early to predict what majorities DAP candidates could regain, given the possibility of a 10 per cent shift in Chinese voter sentiment, as seen in previous state elections in Sabah, Johor and Negri Sembilan.
"At the same time, I expect fierce contests in the two seats currently held by MCA, Machap Jaya and Klebang, both of which have majorities of fewer than 1,000 votes," he said when contacted today.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, PH won five seats, four through DAP and one through Amanah, while PKR failed to win any.
PH was previously reported to be considering cooperation with Bersatu for the 16th Melaka election, with PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari tasked with examining the prospects.
Neither side had made an official announcement as of today. Last night, PH announced it would contest 21 seats, with PKR fielding candidates in nine, DAP in seven and Amanah in five. The remaining seven seats were not announced and were believed to be intended for a coalition partner.
Mohammad Tawfik said experience in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections showed that political cooperation did not necessarily lead to an automatic transfer of votes, including Malay votes.
He said Bersatu's support could not be assumed to transfer directly to PH, and the party's poor performance in the previous Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections could be repeated in Melaka.
"Bersatu's support was previously 'siphoned off' by Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), a breakaway from Bersatu. In Negri Sembilan, for example, Bersatu lost all 24 seats and recovered its election deposit in only one, Jeram Padang.
"In my view, this development is alarming for Bersatu. PH needs to be cautious about this cooperation because it could drain its campaign machinery and financial resources without necessarily improving the chances of winning seats contested by Bersatu," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man dies after being stung by swarm of bees while collecting honey
Article:
KEMAMAN: A man died after being stung by a swarm of bees while trying to collect honey from a tree in Batu 18, Jalan Air Putih, Terengganu yesterday.
Hafizul Mat Nor, 40, was attacked by the bees about 9.50am.
District police chief Superintendent Mohd Razi Rosli said the victim had asked a 44-year-old friend to accompany him to collect the honey.
He said the friend initially told the victim not to take the honey as the tree was very tall, but the victim decided to climb it anyway.
"While climbing the tree, a swarm of bees suddenly attacked and stung the victim.
"At that point, the victim shouted for his friend to run to safety.
"The victim tried to climb back down to save himself, and both of them ran into a pool of water at a nearby plantation," he said in a statement.
Razi said the victim then complained of pain in his legs and arms from the stings before getting out of the water and collapsing.
He said the victim's friend tried to wake him but, on realising he was unconscious and convulsing, immediately called the emergency line.
"The victim's friend immediately sought ambulance assistance before the victim was rushed to Kemaman Hospital for further treatment," he said.
He said the victim was, however, pronounced dead at the hospital at 6.42pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 12,500ha of Kelantan padi fields face flood risk during monsoon
Article:
KOTA BARU: About 12,500 ha of padi fields under the Kemubu Agricultural Development Authority (Kada) scheduled for harvesting in November and December face flood risks during the Northeast Monsoon.
Kada chairman Khalid Abdul Samad said 56 per cent of the 25,000 ha of padi cultivation areas under the agency had been harvested for the first season of 2026 as of today.
"The remaining 44 per cent includes 11,000 ha scheduled for harvesting next month and another 1,500 ha in December, mainly in the Tumpat area. These areas could be affected if flooding occurs during the period," he said.
He said Kada implemented five monsoon preparedness measures, including maintaining drainage systems, coordinating water gate operations, operating seven active drainage pumps, scheduling the second padi planting season, and relocating assets to safer areas.
Khalid said this after the launch of the 2026 Integrity Day celebration and the Kada Corruption-Free Pledge ceremony here today.
Meanwhile, Khalid said Kada considered the average deduction rate of about 23 per cent for moisture and impurities during the first 2026 harvest season to be reasonable, adding that no complaints had been received from farmers.
He said that as of Oct 18, average deduction rates varied among Area Farmers' Organisations (PPK), with PPK Jaya Peringat recording 23 per cent, followed by PPK Sri Gunong at 23.5 per cent and PPK Tanjong Puri at 24.5 per cent.
He said Kada will monitor the padi grading process and investigate any complaints about deductions deemed excessive or unreasonable.
Padi farmers were also advised to follow the established planting schedule to avoid harvesting during the monsoon season, which could affect padi quality and result in higher deduction rates.
Khalid said grading was based on the quality of padi delivered to mills, including the presence of foreign matter, empty grains, damaged or immature grains, and excessive moisture content. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mah Sing targets 30pct recurring revenue in strategic business shift
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mah Sing Group Bhd aims to derive 30 per cent of its group revenue from recurring income within the next five years as it diversifies its earnings base beyond property sales and expands its industrial and data centre-related opportunities.
The target represents a shift towards a more diversified earnings model, reducing reliance on property sales while building a stronger base of income from leasing commercial properties, estates and retail space.
Mah Sing founder and group managing director Tan Sri Leong Hoy Kum said recurring income, although currently contributing a relatively small share of revenue, would become an increasingly important part of the group's long-term growth strategy.
"The recurring-income ambition is part of Mah Sing's longer-term growth plans, although achieving the 30 per cent contribution will depend on expanding its income-generating portfolio and converting opportunities into sustainable revenue," he told Business Times.
Leong said the company's current priority was to grow the business and continue improving performance, with recurring income, industrial developments and land monetisation offering potential avenues to strengthen its earnings base.
Mah Sing is also exploring land sales to data centre operators and hyperscalers in Johor to capitalise on growing demand for digital infrastructure.
Its industrial property push includes MS Industrial Park @ Kulai, a RM2.2 billion joint-venture development with KLK Land Sdn Bhd spanning 419.17 acres of freehold land within Zone E of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
The partners have opened the project's sales gallery after Phase 1A recorded more than 90 per cent take-up, with Phase 1B now open for sale.
Planned across five phases, the industrial park will offer two-storey semi-detached and detached factories, industrial land parcels ranging from one to eight acres, and larger plots for customised industrial facilities and data centre developments.
Mah Sing holds a 60 per cent stake in the project, while KLK Land, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, owns the remaining 40 per cent.
Since entering Johor in 2000, Leong said the group has continued to grow its presence through residential and industrial developments.
"Our experience in developing five industrial parks across the Greater Klang Valley and Johor gives us a solid foundation as we embark on MS Industrial Park @ Kulai, our sixth industrial development. We see strong potential in Kulai, supported by the JS-SEZ, its proximity to Singapore, improving infrastructure and the continued growth of high-value industries in Johor," he said in a statement.
Meanwhile, Mah Sing plans to introduce higher-end residential products next year while maintaining its focus on homes within its established price range. Further development announcements are also expected next year.
Leong said the group's immediate priority remained growing the business and improving performance across its property segments.
Mah Sing is targeting property sales of RM2.76 billion this year after posting an eight per cent increase in net profit for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY2025).
Net profit rose to RM260 million from RM239.1 million a year earlier, supported by the finalisation of construction costs for projects nearing completion.
