Title: Damaged Kuala Besar jetty puts more than 1,000 users at risk
Article:
KOTA BARU: More than 1,000 people who travel daily between Kuala Besar and the islands off Tumpat face safety risks due to a badly damaged jetty they rely on to board boats.
Damaged by floods last year, the jetty has been left with broken railings and a damaged platform, raising concerns over the safety of residents and visitors travelling to islands including Pulau Suri.
Residents have resorted to placing stones beneath broken sections of the structure in an attempt to support the platform and keep the jetty usable.
Kampung Che Latiff head Wan Kamal Wan Ahmad, 61, who has served as village head for three years, said the jetty was built with federal government funding more than three years ago and had become a vital link for island communities.
He said it was used by residents, visitors and authorities, particularly during emergencies and when transporting patients to the mainland for medical treatment.
"The jetty is our main access point to the islands. It is used by residents and the authorities, including when patients need to be taken to hospital by boat before being transferred by ambulance.
"Some people have been injured after falling at the damaged jetty. We are worried that someone could suffer more serious injuries if the situation continues," he said.
Wan Kamal said residents hoped the authorities would repair or replace the structure as soon as possible.
"If possible, we hope a concrete jetty can be built to provide a safer and more durable facility for the people," said the father of three.
He said the jetty operated around the clock and served more than 60 passenger boats and 22 privately owned boats. A parking area was also available at no charge.
"The current platform is made of fibreglass, but the damaged structure remains a major concern for us," he added.
Resident Hassan Bakar, 62, said the jetty's condition was a daily concern for communities whose lives revolved around boat travel.
The father of three said thousands of people living on the islands relied on boats for their daily journeys.
Hassan said the combined population of Pulau Rejuna and Pulau Suri was about 5,000, while the wider island community had an estimated population of 10,000. However, residents of other islands use separate jetties.
Boat fares range from RM2 to RM3 per passenger, while children travel free, he said.
"The journey between the mainland and the islands takes about five to 10 minutes, making the jetty a vital link for residents travelling for work, education, medical treatment and other daily needs.
"Therefore, I believe a proper jetty is important. If necessary, a concrete jetty," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid outlines 3 TVET initiatives for rural youth
Article:
SUNGAI BESAR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has outlined three technical and vocational education and training (TVET) initiatives to produce skilled workers and entrepreneurs among rural youth.
The initiatives are the TVET Premium Career Agreement, TVET Jana Desa and Smart and Green TVET Workshops, which will be implemented in phases.
Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the TVET Premium Career Agreement would prioritise early cooperation with employers in selected programmes, including agreements on competencies, placement conditions and salary packages before trainees are recruited.
He said industry players would also be involved in curriculum development and assessments to ensure training met labour market needs.
"This approach is intended to improve job matching, ensure appropriate starting salaries and provide clearer career progression pathways for TVET graduates," he said.
He was speaking at the opening of the TVET Expo at Stadium Sungai Besar.
Zahid said the second initiative, TVET Jana Desa, aimed to produce graduates capable of establishing technical enterprises and creating jobs in their respective districts.
Fields such as agricultural machinery maintenance, pumps and cooling systems had local economic potential in areas such as Sungai Besar, he said.
"Graduates will receive business guidance, access to financing and market opportunities so that their technical skills can be developed into enterprises capable of creating jobs for local communities," he said.
Under the Smart and Green TVET Workshops initiative, workshops at TVET institutions will serve as collaborative spaces for trainees, instructors and industry players to develop practical technological solutions.
Zahid said projects being considered included machine monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI)-based automation and energy efficiency to help rural entrepreneurs increase productivity and reduce operating costs.
He said the initiatives would also complement the 2027 Budget target of placing 1,000 Bumiputera youths in high-growth sectors through Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA), as well as using GiatMARA wiring skills to carry out wiring repairs in 20,000 homes belonging to poor families.
"The Ministry of Rural and Regional Development, together with implementing agencies and industry partners, will also detail the institutions involved, financing mechanisms and outcome targets to ensure implementation of each initiative can be monitored and its benefits reach the intended groups," he said.
Zahid urged young people to seize TVET opportunities by choosing their fields of study seriously, developing their skills to a high level of expertise and upholding integrity at work.
He also called on parents to support their children in choosing TVET as a pathway to their futures.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian woman rescued after falling into 10m-deep hole in Vietnam
Article:
LAM DONG, Vietnam: A 40-year-old Malaysian woman was rescued after falling into a 10m-deep hole while hiking in Da Lat, Lam Dong, on Sunday, the Vietnam News Agency reported.
The incident occurred at 5.45am in the Hon Bo mountain area of Lam Vien-Da Lat ward.
The woman, identified by her initials G.S.W., was hiking in the area when she fell into a hole about 70cm in diameter, said to be part of an abandoned mining site.
She became trapped inside the hole, and attempts by others in the hiking group to pull her out were unsuccessful. Local authorities were alerted to launch an emergency rescue operation.
Rescuers successfully brought the woman out of the hole at 7.15am and took her to Lam Dong General Hospital for emergency treatment.
Initial reports indicated she had sustained an injury to her right ankle. She received first aid before being transferred to the hospital for further treatment.
Hon Bo Mountain, near Thai Phien flower village in Da Lat, is a popular destination for hiking, cloud hunting, and photography, attracting both residents and tourists.
The mountain offers scenic views towards Da Lat's centre, particularly in the early morning. However, spontaneous hiking and sightseeing in the area can pose safety risks, especially for visitors unfamiliar with the local terrain.
Authorities advised visitors to exercise caution when exploring mountainous areas and to avoid hiking independently in locations where the terrain and potential hazards are unfamiliar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mislabelled palm oil blends could hurt Malaysia’s reputation abroad, Maritime experts say
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Palm oil blended in Malaysia must carry accurate declarations of origin, as any inaccuracy could undermine the integrity and reputation of Malaysian products in international markets, a maritime expert said.
Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) Faculty of Maritime Studies senior lecturer Dr Madzli Harun said that while palm oil blending was permitted in the industry, the process did not automatically make the finished product Malaysian in origin.
He said a product’s country of origin was determined under the applicable Rules of Origin (RoO), which take into account processing methods, raw material content and criteria set out under the relevant trade regulations.
“If the original bill of lading (B/L) states that the refined, bleached and deodorised (RBD) palm olein originates from Indonesia, subsequently blending the product in Malaysia does not automatically make it a Malaysian-origin product.
“The B/L may be amended after a vessel leaves the port of loading and while it is sailing to the port of destination, but such amendments must be supported by reasonable grounds and valid documentation,” he said.
Madzli said blending alone might not satisfy RoO requirements or change a product’s country of origin, and operators must therefore show that the processing carried out meets the relevant criteria before the finished product can be declared Malaysian in origin.
“In the Asean context, the Asean Trade in Goods Agreement (Atiga) sets out rules of origin that include criteria such as Regional Value Content (RVC), change in tariff classification and cumulation.
“The use of raw materials from Asean member states may be taken into account when determining the origin of a finished product under certain circumstances, subject to the requirements of the agreement.
“Operators cannot simply blend oil from Indonesia with Malaysian oil and then label it ‘Made in Malaysia’. The finished product must meet the prescribed requirements before it can qualify for recognition as Malaysian-origin,” he said.
He said the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMCD), the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) and the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) should examine the relevant documentation within their respective jurisdictions to ensure blending activities and origin declarations complied with the applicable regulations.
“The documents that need to be examined include import and export records, certificates of origin, the quantity of imported oil, the volume of Malaysian oil used and records of the blending process.
“Traceability is also important to ensure that the origin of raw materials can be identified even after products from different countries have been blended.
“Even if the finished product qualifies for Malaysian-origin status under the applicable rules, records of raw materials imported from Indonesia must still be retained. Information on the origin of those materials must not simply be erased after blending,” he said.
He also warned that if a blended product was found to be contaminated, Malaysia could suffer reputational damage, face cargo rejections by buyers and potentially encounter legal action, depending on the circumstances and the parties responsible.
Madzli said false declarations could also lead to action under the relevant laws, including Section 133 of the Customs Act 1967, if the elements of an offence under the provision were established.
Meanwhile, maritime expert Prof Nazery Khalid said documentation for blended cargoes should accurately reflect the composition and characteristics of the resulting product to avoid doubts about its contents.
He said this was important because if a blended cargo was found to be contaminated and posed a health risk to consumers after export, Malaysia could suffer reputational damage if the product was perceived to have originated from the country.
“The recent food poisoning incident in Taiwan involving contaminated cooking oil should serve as a lesson.
“As one of the world’s major palm oil producers, Malaysia must ensure that its exported oil meets quality and integrity standards, while ensuring that its processing, documentation and shipment are carried out properly,” he said.

Title: Zahid, national leaders extend congratulations to Sultan of Selangor on silver jubilee
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, together with the country’s leaders, has extended his heartfelt congratulations to the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, on the Silver Jubilee of His Royal Highness’ reign today.
In a Facebook post, Ahmad Zahid prayed that Allah would continue to grant Sultan Sharafuddin good health, well-being and strength to continue providing leadership and protection to the people and state of Selangor.
“I pray that Allah SWT will continue to grant Your Royal Highness good health, a blessed life and the strength to continue leading and protecting the state and people of Selangor, with wisdom and compassion for all.
“May the state of Selangor remain peaceful, prosperous and blessed under Your Royal Highness’ reign. Daulat Tuanku!” he said.
Also extending his congratulations was Chief Secretary to the Government, Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, who expressed hope that the Sultan’s patronage would continue to be a source of strength for public servants, in carrying out their responsibilities with loyalty and integrity for the well-being of the people.
“May Your Royal Highness’ patronage continue to be a source of strength for all public servants in carrying out their duties, with loyalty and integrity for the well-being of the people,” he said in a Facebook post.
Meanwhile, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil also prayed that Sultan Sharafuddin and the entire Selangor royal family would always be blessed with good health and well-being.
“I pray that His Royal Highness and the entire Selangor royal family will be blessed with lasting good health and well-being. Daulat Tuanku!” he said in a Facebook post. — Bernama

Title: Sanusi: GE16 will be Pakatan’s last term in Putrajaya and Perikatan’s final term as Opposition
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 25 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has predicted that Pakatan Harapan will lose power in Putrajaya at the 16th general election, according to online reports.
He told supporters that PN must use the time left before GE16, expected by December 2027, to strengthen its election machinery.
“This is Pakatan’s final term governing Malaysia and Perikatan’s final term as the Opposition. After this, we (Perikatan) will form the federal government,” he was quoted as saying by news portal
Kedah Online
at Stadium Sultan Muhammad IV here during a gathering for Muslim unity last Friday.
According to Sanusi, a PN government would take a new approach to national development, “developing together with Islam”.
Sanusi also said the PN leadership will make a decision about its participation in the coming Sarawak state election after the November 14 Melaka polls.
Sarawak’s polling date has yet to be announced, but the state assembly’s five-year term expires in February 2027.
Sarawak minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah has said the polls could be held on December 12 or 19.
Sanusi added that informal talks had been held on synchronising elections in the four PN-ruled states with GE16, but no decision had been finalised.
He urged party members and supporters to work hard, and called on Malaysians who value peace and justice to give PN a chance to form the next government.

Title: No walk-ins: Finas opens RM15m Creative Content Fund applications online only from Nov 16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Applications for the Creative Content Fund (Film Sector), which opens on November 16, must be submitted online through the Creative Industry Management and Monitoring System (SPPIK) portal at
https://sppik.finas.my
.
The National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) said applications would be subject to the prevailing Creative Content Fund guidelines and regulations.
“Applications for all categories must be submitted exclusively through the SPPIK portal at
https://sppik.finas.my
.
“Detailed infographics, application links and video tutorials on the application process will be made available on Finas’ official website and social media platforms when applications open,” it said in a statement today.
The six categories include the International Co-Production Fund for Feature Films/Animated Features, First Time Amateur Film Maker (FAME) Fund and Television Programme Co-Production Fund (Supertelefilm).
The other categories are the Micro-Drama Co-Production Fund (Broadcasting Stations/OTT Platforms), Veteran Artists Supertelefilm (STAR) Fund and National Public Service Announcement (PSA) Production Fund.
For enquiries or further information, applicants may contact Finas’ Production Management Division via email at
infodkd@finas.my
.
Yesterday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the RM15 million Creative Content Fund (DKK), covering six categories under Finas, was aimed at creating opportunities for emerging talent and expanding international collaboration. — Bernama

Title: Dzulkefly: MOH strengthening mental health support nationwide, workplace policy under consultation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is to continue strengthening the support system and access to mental health services nationwide, including through the development of a mental health policy at the workplace, which is currently undergoing an engagement process with stakeholders.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr. Dzulkefly Ahmad said MOH is engaging with the Ministry of Human Resources (KESUMA) and other relevant agencies to ensure the policy is developed comprehensively, taking into account the needs of various parties.
“This process requires broader consultation before the policy can be finalised, to prevent it from being implemented in isolation without sufficient coordination between agencies,” he said during a press conference after officiating the National-Level World Mental Health Month 2026 celebration here today.
MOH is also expanding access to mental health services through 1,116 government health clinics nationwide, in addition to hospitals and community-based services such as Community Mental Health Centres (MENTARI).
He noted that there are approximately 700 registered psychiatrists in Malaysia, with 400 serving within
Dzulkefly added that MOH continues to expand specialised psychiatric training, while also optimising the roles of other healthcare personnel through a “task-shifting” approach.
“This approach also involves over 500 family medicine specialists who provide mental health services at the primary healthcare level,” he said.
There are approximately 300 counselors within the ministry, while a total of 10,000 counselors are registered with the Board of Counselors of Malaysia nationwide.
Additionally, 68 Ministry of Health (MOH) hospitals and four psychiatric institutions provide psychiatric services, bringing the total to 72 facilities.
He said that the involvement of various categories of healthcare personnel allows the public to access assistance and early intervention, without having to rely solely on the services of psychiatrists.
According to him, more than 55,000 civil servants have been identified as being at high risk of mental health issues including suicidal tendencies based on screenings conducted via Civil Servants’ Psychological Health Digital Profile System (MyPsyD).
“The demand of professionalism should not come at the expense of the sanity and well-being of our own workforce,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Man found dead outside Cheras food stall; police say no foul play suspected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Police have classified the death of a man in his mid-20s whose body was discovered outside a food stall in Cheras as a sudden death.
According to
The Star
, the man was found unconscious at Flat Sri Melaka on Jalan Ikan Emas today, according to Cheras OCPD Asst Comm Mohd Rosdi Daud.
“Preliminary investigations found no elements of crime at the scene,” he said in a statement today.
An assistant medical officer from Kuala Lumpur Hospital pronounced the man dead at the scene, Mohd Rosdi added.
Officers from the Criminal Investigation Division, the Salak Selatan police station and the police forensic team were sent to the location promptly, he said.
The cause of death has yet to be established and will require confirmation through a post-mortem.
The body was taken to the forensic unit at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz in Cheras for further action.
Mohd Rosdi said investigations are ongoing.

Title: Mardi worker killed by bee swarm while collecting honey at farm in Kemaman
Article:
CHUKAI, Oct 25 — A Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Mardi) staff member died after being stung by a swarm of bees while collecting honey at the agency’s farm in Ayer Putih near here yesterday.
Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said the incident occurred at 9.50am when the victim, Hafizul Mat, 40, a general worker, was at MARDI’s Kemaman branch at Kilometer 18 of Jalan Ayer Putih with a colleague.
“The victim’s 44-year-old colleague had advised him against collecting the honey because the beehive was on a dry tree about three metres tall, but the victim insisted on proceeding.
“The victim asked his colleague to wait about 50 metres from the beehive before climbing the tree to collect the honey, but he was attacked by a swarm of bees,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Razi said that while in the tree, the victim shouted at his colleague to run as the bees swarmed him. He then climbed down and jumped into a nearby pool of water to avoid being stung.
Mohd Razi said the victim later complained of pain in his arms and legs from the stings before getting out of the pool and collapsing unconscious with convulsions.
“The victim’s colleague then sought help from two other co-workers before calling an ambulance. The victim was taken to Kemaman Hospital for further treatment,” he said.
However, Mohd Razi said the hospital confirmed that the victim died while receiving treatment at 6.42pm. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain in Labuan and six states until 9pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Labuan and six states until 9pm tonight.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the areas affected in Kelantan are Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Tumpat, Pasir Mas and Machang, while in Pahang, they are Jerantut, Kuantan, Maran, Pekan and Lipis.
The warning also covers Terengganu, Johor and Sarawak, including Song in Kapit; Kanowit and Sibu in Sibu; Julau and Pakan in Sarikei; Lubok Antu in Sri Aman; Serian; Betong; and Kuching.
In Sabah, the affected areas are the Interior, West Coast and Kudat divisions, as well as Paitan, Telupid, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Tongod in the Sandakan division, and Kalabakan in the Tawau division. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Eight areas nationwide record unhealthy API as of 6pm, Serian highest at 192
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Eight areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 6pm today, with Serian IPD in Sarawak recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 192.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five other monitoring stations in Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings, namely Kuching (180), Samarahan (177), Sri Aman (157), Sibu (152) and Sarikei (109).
Unhealthy API readings were also recorded in Terengganu, with Paka registering 156, while Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded 152.
Meanwhile, APIMS reported that 50 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 10 areas remained at the good level.
API readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are classified as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Police seek dashcam footage, urge witnesses to come forward after crash involving Bernama, NST journalists
Article:
IPOH, Oct 25 — The police are urging members of the public who witnessed an accident involving a car carrying two journalists and a lorry which occurred this morning on Jalan Ipoh-Lumut, near the Taman Kledang Permai traffic light junction to come forward and assist with the investigation.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those who possess dashcam footage of the incident are also requested to provide the information to the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Ipoh district police headquarters (IPD).
He noted that the incident, which took place at approximately 5.45 am., involved a Perodua Bezza carrying the two journalists, who were traveling from the direction of Meru towards Bagan Datuk.
“Upon reaching the scene, the car which had stopped at a traffic light intersection was struck from behind by a lorry traveling in the same direction.
“As a result of the collision, the car spun on the road, while the lorry veered off and ended up in a roadside drain,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Alwi said police received a report regarding the incident at 8.38 am, and three victims were transported to Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital (HRPB) here for further medical treatment.
Earlier, two journalists who were en route to cover an event involving Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr. Ahmad Zahid Hamidi in Bagan Datuk today sustained injuries in the accident.
Nur Afiradina Arshad, 34, a journalist with the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), is currently receiving treatment in the ‘yellow zone’ (semi-critical area) at HRPB, while Zahratulhayat Mat Arif, 37, a journalist of the New Straits Times (NST), was discharged following treatment.
Mohd Alwi added that further investigations into the incident are ongoing. — Bernama

Title: No piranha found or caught at Klau Dam, but presence not ruled out, says Fisheries Dept
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 25 — No piranha fish were found or caught during the Alien Fish Mitigation Programme at the Klau Dam, Raub, which took place over two days starting yesterday, said Fisheries Director-General Datuk Adnan Hussain.
However, this situation cannot be interpreted as proof that the species is no longer present in the dam, following previous reports confirming the discovery of piranhas in the area.
He said this mitigation program is one of the inland fisheries management efforts to control alien fish populations and reduce the risk of disruption to native fish species.
“No piranha fish were found or caught throughout this program. However, monitoring and scientific assessment must continue to identify the presence and distribution of the species,” he said via a media statement today.
Previously, a video went viral on social media regarding the discovery of a fish allegedly resembling a piranha at the Klau Dam, Raub, sparking various reactions from the public.
The Department of Fisheries (DOF) added in the same release that, apart from catching activities, research using the environmental DNA (eDNA) method was also carried out during this programme to help detect the possible presence of piranhas in the Klau Dam.
This method allows water samples to be analysed to detect genetic material that may have been left behind by aquatic organisms.
“The final results of the eDNA research will be determined after the analysis and scientific evaluation process is completed. Therefore, any conclusion regarding the status of piranha presence in the Klau Dam must take into account these analysis results alongside relevant monitoring information and field evidence,” according to the statement.
The DOF informed that this programme also aims to reduce the alien fish population, assess the fish composition in the dam’s waters, and increase public awareness of the threat posed by alien species to aquatic biodiversity and ecosystem balance.
The programme, conducted at the approximately 25-square-kilometer dam, involved 150 participants, consisting of 100 anglers, 32 cast-net participants, and 18 gill-net participants.
“Throughout the programme, a total of 156.6 kilograms of alien fish were recorded, involving three main groups, namely Peacock Bass, Zebra Tilapia, and Javanese Carp (Lampam Jawa),” according to the statement. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Johor schools to reopen in phases, starting with exam candidates
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 25 — Schools in Johor will reopen in phases, with the first phase on Monday (tomorrow) and Tuesday limited to students sitting for examinations according to the scheduled timetable.
State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made following the decree of the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, who places great importance on the safety, health and well-being of the people of Johor.
He said the arrangement would also give school administrators and teachers time to prepare for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Ujian Akhir Sesi Akademik (UASA) examinations.
“The second phase will begin on Wednesday, when all schools throughout Johor are scheduled to resume full operations as usual, subject to developments in air quality,” he said in a statement today.
Muhammad Naqib said the Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) would coordinate the implementation of health and safety standard operating procedures (SOPs), including the wearing of face masks and monitoring of school activities, based on current air pollutant index (API) readings.
He said the state government and relevant agencies would continue to monitor the haze situation closely to ensure that any necessary action could be taken based on assessments of prevailing conditions.
Yesterday, the Johor state government decided that all educational institutions would resume operations tomorrow after taking into account developments in the haze situation and assessments by the relevant agencies.
As of 4 pm today, only two districts in Johor recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Pasir Gudang at 154 and Batu Pahat at 127. — Bernama

Title: Johor expects 26,000 job opportunities for youth this year, says Onn Hafiz
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 25 — The Johor government expects 26,000 job opportunities to be offered to young people across the state this year, driven by rapid economic growth and the influx of high-value investments.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the projected figure reflected a consistent year-on-year increase, following the success of various strategic initiatives, including the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and large-scale career events such as the Johor Talent Development Council (JTDC) Mega Job Fair.
He said the state had continued to record a significant increase in quality job opportunities compared with previous years.
“A total of 15,000 job opportunities were offered in 2022, rising to 17,000 in 2024 and surging to 24,000 in 2025, before reaching a target of 26,000 this year,” he said.
“For comparison, the JTDC Mega Job Fair alone offered 3,000 job opportunities, 30 per cent of which, or 1,000 positions, were in the premium-salary category,” he said when delivering his speech at the closing ceremony of the JTDC Mega Job Fair at the Tunku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre (TMIYC) in Iskandar Puteri here today.
Elaborating further, Onn Hafiz said Johor’s strong economic performance was also supported by a gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate of 8 per cent, the highest in the country’s history, as well as investment inflows reaching RM110 billion.
However, he said these macroeconomic growth figures must translate into tangible benefits for the people, particularly young people and small and medium enterprises (SMEs), so that they could genuinely share in the state’s prosperity.
“These figures must not simply look good on paper; the people must feel and enjoy the benefits of the development taking place in the state,” he said.
In line with efforts to strengthen human capital, he said the state government was also emphasising the importance of reskilling and upskilling programmes to ensure the local workforce met the standards required by high-paying industries in advanced manufacturing, logistics, energy and data centres. — Bernama

Title: Four Bangladeshis among six held in Sungai Petani over online gaming scam, syndicate ran from abandoned hotel
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 25 — Police recently arrested six individuals, including four Bangladeshi men, suspected of being involved in an online gaming scam syndicate.
Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the syndicate, which operated from an abandoned hotel in Taman Lagenda near here, was believed to have been active since June.
“In a raid at 9.30pm on Wednesday (October 21), a team of officers and personnel from the Kuala Muda District Police Headquarters (IPD) Commercial Crime Investigation Division (CCID) arrested four Bangladeshi men aged between 20 and 53.
“The group targeted victims among the Bangladesh community. They are believed to have received salaries of about RM2,700 per month to carry out the activities,” he told a press conference at the Kuala Muda IPD here today.
Hanyan said further investigations led to the arrest of two Malaysian men aged 40 and 50 in a raid on Friday (October 23), adding that they were believed to be the premises owner and an agent who handled the process of renting the premises to the suspects.
The syndicate is believed to have handled online game credit top-ups and used a website and WhatsApp to communicate with customers.
“Customers’ withdrawals of their winnings were deliberately delayed, with the status shown as ‘pending withdrawal’, resulting in them not receiving the money.
“Based on preliminary information, about 17 customer accounts a day were believed to have encountered the problem, with estimated losses of around RM2,000 a day,” he said.
Hanyan said police seized various items, including 17 mobile phones, four computer processing units (CPUs), eight monitors, two modems, a laptop and RM2,442 in cash.
Further investigations are ongoing under Sections 420 and 120B of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: PKR’s seven new faces must earn voters’ trust, says Adam Adli
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 25 — Melaka PKR is fielding seven new faces among its nine candidates for next month’s state election, as the party seeks to strengthen support for its reform agenda at the state level.
State party acting chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said PKR needs to work hard to convince voters of the principles and reform agenda it was pursuing at the federal level and ensure they gain acceptance in Melaka.
“Winning the seats contested depends not only on the candidates’ names or personal appeal, but also on their relationships with the community, the strength of their campaign machinery and the agenda they offer.
“Everyone contests an election to win, but candidates must ensure their messages are conveyed effectively to the people throughout the campaign period, while making the interests of the community and voters their top priority,” he told reporters here today.
He was speaking after officiating at the Madani Kita programme with the Ayer Keroh community at Hang Tuah Jaya, held at the Sungai Putat People’s Housing Project (PPR) multipurpose hall in Batu Berendam.
Adam Adli, who is also a member of the party’s Central Leadership Council, said PKR candidates must also demonstrate a commitment to good governance and uphold high standards of conduct and personal integrity when engaging with the community.
Last night, Prime Minister and Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the coalition’s 21 candidates for the state election, comprising nine from PKR, seven from DAP and five from Amanah.
The seven new faces fielded by PKR are Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri in Tanjung Bidara, Mohd Khuzairie Mohd Kamal Kannan in Rembia, P Denesh in Asahan, Datuk Azman Abidin in Paya Rumput, Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar in Ayer Molek, Esma Eazreen Husin in Rim and Muhammad Faiq Azman in Serkam.
The two candidates with previous election experience are Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir in Kelebang and Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin in Machap Jaya. — Bernama

Title: Haze: 27 schools in Tebedu to close tomorrow, says Sarawak Education Dept
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 25 — Twenty-seven schools in the Tebedu district of Serian will be closed tomorrow due to haze, following continuous monitoring of Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and reports from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
The Sarawak State Education Department (JPN) said the Oct 26 closure would involve one secondary school and 26 primary schools under its supervision.
“During the closure, Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) will be implemented, while teachers and Support Staff Group (AKP) will bellowed to work from home (WFH),” the JPN said in a statement today.
It added that the closure decision would also apply to all primary and secondary schools in districts recording API readings above 200 after the statement was issued.
However, face-to-face classes for Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates would continue, subject to the wearing of face masks in accordance with examination management guidelines during disasters and haze.
The Sarawak JPN said that for schools near districts with API readings exceeding 200, headmasters and principals could consider implementing PdPR by taking into account students’ health and safety.
It also said that preparations to reopen schools could be made if the API readings showed a downward trend to below 200.
All educational institutions under the department’s supervision are also reminded to monitor API readings through the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, and comply with advice from the Ministry of Health to protect the health of students and members of the education community.
Meanwhile, parents and guardians would be allowed to keep their children at home if they are concerned about the impact of the haze on their health, provided they inform the school.
Sarawak JPN also stressed that the health, safety and well-being of everyone in the education community remained its top priority. — Bernama

Title: IGP: Police identify suspects linked to 1.16-tonne ketamine haul found on Malaysian-owned tanker in Indonesian waters
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — Police have identified several individuals suspected of being linked to the attempted smuggling of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine found aboard a Malaysian-owned tanker in Indonesian waters recently.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police were tracking down the individuals and would strive to make arrests as soon as possible, either today or tomorrow.
“We have identified the individuals and are trying to locate them. The companies and those linked to the case are also known to us,” he told the media after attending the 26th convocation ceremony of Spectrum International University College here today.
Mohd Khalid said investigations found that the vessel had departed from Johor for Port Klang before heading towards the Andaman Sea, which is believed to be where the ship-to-ship transfer took place.
He said the vessel’s decision to turn back and enter Indonesian waters provided the authorities there with an opportunity to conduct investigations and make arrests.
In this regard, he said Malaysia would continue to cooperate with the Indonesian authorities to ensure that all those involved were brought to justice.
Mohd Khalid said he had been informed that the vessel was owned by Malaysians but registered in Mongolia.
He said more information was still needed to assist the investigation, including matters concerning ownership of the vessel, as the case involved a very large quantity of drugs.
The media reported that the tanker, MT Global 168, was intercepted off Tanjung Balai Asahan, North Sumatra, on October 20. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina orders probe, removes Perak principal from school amid harassment allegations
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has directed the Perak Education Department (JPN) to investigate allegations that a school principal sexually harassed a student.
She said the principal has also been temporarily reassigned to the Bagan Datuk District Education Office (PPD) pending the outcome of the investigation, as reported by
Harian Metro
(HM).
“The Perak JPN has been instructed to conduct an investigation. The principal has also been placed temporarily at the Bagan Datuk PPD until the investigation is completed,” Fadhlina was quoted as saying.
Her response came after a viral social media post warned parents and residents in Teluk Intan to remain vigilant following allegations involving a principal at a government secondary school.
The post alleged that the principal had sexually harassed a Form Three female student, including by sending her romantic messages, and also made claims of an inappropriate relationship.
It urged the authorities and the public to treat the matter seriously, calling for a thorough investigation in the interest of student safety.

Title: FT008 detour near Gua Musang now open to light traffic after sinkhole
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 25 — A temporary detour at FT008 Section 205.556 along the Gua Musang-Kota Bharu road near the Kesedar Ethnobotanical Recreation Park here was opened to light vehicles at noon today.
In a statement, the Gua Musang Public Works Department (JKR) said the detour, built using a Bailey bridge, was constructed at the site of a sinkhole on the road.
The detour, which is part of the Central Spine Road (LTU) Project Packages 3B and 3C, is open only to light vehicles.
Road users have been advised to follow temporary traffic signs and safety instructions, reduce their speed and exercise caution when passing through the area.
They should also plan their journeys in advance, while heavy vehicles are advised to use alternative routes.
The FT008 federal road near Kesedar Ethnobotanical Recreation Park was closed on Oct 10 following the formation of a sinkhole about eight metres deep. — Bernama

Title: Takiyuddin: Bersatu invited to Perikatan talks on RoS case, Melaka polls
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will discuss its legal challenge against the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over the coalition’s suspension, as well as preparations for the Melaka state election, at a meeting in Kuala Lumpur tonight.
According to
News Straits Times
(NST), PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said Bersatu leaders had been invited to attend the meeting at PAS headquarters, but whether they would do so was up to them.
He said the allocation of the seven seats assigned to PN for the Melaka polls would also be discussed.
According to Takiyuddin, the seats will be distributed among the coalition’s component parties, with Bersatu excluded after deciding to contest under its own logo.
He said the limited number of seats available meant PN would need to work out a suitable distribution among the parties involved.

Title: IGP orders immediate CID probe into Noorizwan’s death in custody
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has directed the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to conduct an immediate investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died while in police custody at the Cheras District Police Headquarters (IPD).
He said the investigation must be conducted thoroughly following the discovery of several unusual injuries on Noorizwan’s body that warranted further scrutiny.
“I have asked the CID, particularly its director Datuk M. Kumar, to investigate this case as soon as possible and make the findings of the investigation known to the public.
“At the same time, once we receive the post-mortem report from the hospital stating the cause of death, we will issue an official statement on the next course of action,” he told reporters after the 26th convocation ceremony of Spectrum International University College (SIUC) here today.
Mohd Khalid said the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department (JIPS), which is responsible for investigating deaths in custody classified as sudden death reports, had issued a statement on the case.
However, police were still awaiting the laboratory report to determine the actual cause of Noorizwan’s death, he added.
Earlier, Bukit Aman JIPS director Datuk Aida Abdul Hamid was reported as saying that the post-mortem found no injuries to Noorizwan’s internal organs, with forensic examination identifying only external injuries on his body.
Noorizwan, 42, died on October 1 after reportedly being brought from the Cheras District Police Headquarters to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz in Cheras the previous day. — Bernama

Title: Melaka state polls: PKR’s 30pc women candidates offer voters a more inclusive choice, says Fadhlina
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL, Oct 25 — PKR’s move to field 30 per cent women candidates in the Melaka state election is part of the party’s strategy to offer voters a more inclusive choice, said Wanita PKR chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said fielding more women candidates could also strengthen women’s representation in state politics.
“I think this is also a good offering for the people to make their choice, particularly in our efforts to continue elevating women as candidates for the Melaka State Legislative Assembly,” she told reporters after officiating at the Nibong Tebal parliamentary constituency-level Jelajah Negaraku: Aku Kasih Malaysia programme here today.
Fadhlina, who is also Education Minister, said that Pakatan Harapan (PH) had also launched the slogan “Melaka Rumah Kita” (Melaka, Our Home) as part of the coalition’s approach to contesting the election.
Yesterday, PH chairman and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced 21 candidates to contest in the Melaka state election.
The Election Commission has set October 31 for nomination day, November 10 for early voting and November 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election. — Bernama

Title: A split second, a lifetime of loss: Family recalls fatal Paya Terubong landslide
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — A 73-year-old doctor was killed when a landslide struck his family's home in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, trapping him beneath collapsed concrete.
The victim, identified as Wong Kar Lin, died when a landslide hit the family’s residence at about 8.36am, trapping him beneath rubble in the kitchen while other family members managed to flee.
Speaking at the scene, Wong’s mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, who is in her 80s, recalled the terrifying moments leading up to the incident,
Berita Harian
(BH) reported
She said she had been taking a shower in an upstairs bathroom when her daughter, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, alerted her to the landslide.
“We were shocked and immediately ran outside to save ourselves. Everything happened so quickly,” she told BH.
However, by the time they reached the ground floor, they discovered that Wong had already been pinned beneath collapsed concrete.
Poh Lim said only the three of them were at home when the landslide occurred, while the couple’s four children live elsewhere.
She described Wong as a devoted son-in-law, adding that his loss was especially painful after more than 30 years together under the same roof.
Although both she and her daughter escaped unhurt, she said she remained deeply shaken by the tragedy.
For Chang, the loss of her husband was difficult to put into words. She said she was nevertheless relieved that rescuers managed to recover Wong's body intact from beneath the rubble.
Fire and Rescue Department personnel retrieved Wong’s body at about 11.21am, nearly three hours after the landslide struck.

Title: Malaysian hiker rescued after falling into 10m-deep hole in Da Lat, Vietnam
Article:
LAM DONG (Vietnam), Oct 25 — A 40-year-old Malaysian woman was rescued after falling into a 10m-deep hole while hiking in Da Lat, Lam Dong, today, the Vietnam News Agency (VNA) reported, citing local authorities.
The incident occurred at around 5.45am in the Hon Bo mountain area of Lam Vien–Da Lat ward, when the woman, identified by her initials G.S.W., was hiking in the area and fell into a hole, said to be part of an abandoned mining site, about 70cm in diameter.
She became trapped inside the hole; the others in the hiking group tried to pull her out but to no avail. Local authorities were called and decided to launch an emergency rescue operation.
Lam Vien–Da Lat ward coordinated with local forces and the Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Rescue Police Division under the provincial Department of Public Security to aid the tourist.
Rescuers successfully brought the woman out of the hole at around 7.15am and took her to Lam Dong General Hospital for emergency treatment.
Initial information indicated that she had sustained an injury to her right ankle. She received first aid before being transferred to the hospital for further treatment.
Hon Bo Mountain, near Thai Phien flower village in Da Lat, is a popular destination for hiking, cloud hunting and photography, attracting both local residents and tourists.
The mountain offers scenic views towards Da Lat’s centre, particularly in the early morning. However, spontaneous hiking and sightseeing in the area can pose safety risks, especially for visitors unfamiliar with the local terrain.
Authorities have advised that visitors exercise caution when exploring mountainous areas and avoid hiking independently in locations where the terrain and potential hazards are unfamiliar. — Bernama-VNA

Title: Melaka cafe gig death: Police reclassify case as murder after delivery rider dies; 10 detained
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 25 — Police have reclassified the death of a delivery rider who was seriously injured while attending a gig at a cafe in Kampung Jawa here on October 17 as a murder case under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Melaka Tengah police chief ACP Halim Abas said the case was initially investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt using a weapon or dangerous object.
“On Oct 17, the victim, a 21-year-old man, was seriously injured while at the cafe to watch a gig. He was later taken to Melaka Hospital for treatment before being placed in intensive care.
“The victim, however, was pronounced dead at 3.53pm on October 21 due to serious injuries to the back of the head in the incident,” he said in a statement here today.
He said police detained 10 individuals aged 18 to 25 on October 18 and 19 to assist in their investigations.
The gig reportedly did not have a permit from the police or local authorities, and investigations into how the event was organised are ongoing.
Previously, claims of a death during a gig at a cafe in Kampung Jawa went viral on social media platform Threads. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina says RM2,500 allowance for Form Six students to begin in first semester next year
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL, Oct 25 — Form Six students will receive RM2,500 in living allowances starting from the first semester next year, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said the allowances, announced under Budget 2027, would be disbursed after the registration process for all Form Six students had been completed.
“Once the registration process for all Form Six students is completed, we will disburse the assistance in their first semester,” she told reporters after officiating at the Nibong Tebal parliamentary constituency-level ‘Jelajah Negaraku: Aku Kasih Malaysia’ programme here today.
She said the allowance would be distributed in stages over the three semesters of study, with approximately RM800 allocated for each semester.
Fadhlina said the initiative demonstrated the government’s commitment to supporting the needs of Form Six students, particularly in their studies, while also improving the quality of Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM).
Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on Oct 9, announced that the government had agreed to provide Form Six students with RM2,500 in living allowances.
The amount is equivalent to the allowance received by matriculation students and is expected to benefit 90,000 Form Six students nationwide.
The provision of the allowance was one of 12 resolutions raised at the Madani Pre-University Congress held in Klang, Selangor, last August. — Bernama

Title: Trade Ministry puts the squeeze on uncertified squishy toys, seizes over 5,800 nationwide
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) seized 5,801 squishy toys worth RM70,428 nationwide for failing to display the required Safety Compliance Mark.
KPDN Enforcement director-general Datuk Azman Adam said the seizures stemmed from 15 enforcement actions during a Special Inspection on Squishy Toys conducted from October 1 to 14 to ensure compliance with child toy safety standards.
“A total of 1,845 premises were inspected, involving manufacturers, importers, wholesalers and retailers.
“KPDN views child toy safety seriously and will not compromise with any party that fails to comply with regulations under the Consumer Protection Act 1999 (Act 599),” he said in a statement today.
He also advised the public, particularly parents, to always check labels and safety compliance marks before buying toys for their children.
Consumers with information on the sale of suspicious toys can lodge complaints via WhatsApp at 019-848 8000 or 019-279 4317; the KPDN e-Aduan portal at e-aduan.kpdn.gov.my; the KPDN Call Centre at 1-800-886-800; or the Ez ADU KPDN smartphone app.
On a separate case, he said a trader was fined RM1,000 by the Putrajaya Magistrates’ Court last Thursday after pleading guilty to making a misleading representation in an advertisement.
He said KPDN had received a complaint from a customer, who had received a jubah instead of a baju kurung as advertised.
“Following the incident on February 27, 2024, an investigation was carried out, which led to the individual’s prosecution in court,” he said.
He said the accused was charged under Section 10(1)(a) of the Consumer Protection Act 1999 [Act 599] and was liable to be punished under Section 25(1)(b) of the same Act. The trader paid the fine. — Bernama

Title: Grandparents, two grandchildren among four killed after Ford hits stranded tow truck on PLUS near Yong Peng
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 25 — Police have confirmed the identities of four people, including two children, who were killed in a three-vehicle accident at KM107 of the North-South Expressway (southbound), near Yong Peng, yesterday.
Batu Pahat police chief ACP Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the 5.50pm incident involved a Ford Ranger, a Toyota Vios and a Scania tow truck.
He said the four victims were passengers in the four-wheel-drive vehicle. They were Ab Shukor Athan, 68, and his wife, Mariam Ibrahim, 65, of Taman Sri Lalang Baru, Kluang, and their two grandchildren, Nur Umie Zahiyah Jumie, 5, and her brother Muhammad Zaharil Hakimie, 1, of Taman Mutiara Rini, Skudai.
“Ab Shukor, Mariam and Nur Umie Zahiyah were pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel from the Yong Peng Health Clinic due to severe head injuries.
“Muhammad Zaharil Hakimie died while receiving treatment at the Parit Yaani Health Clinic,” he said in a statement today.
Shahrulanuar said the accident also left four other occupants of the Ford Ranger with severe head injuries, including its driver, Jumie Julong, 35; his wife, Nor Hakimah Zakiah Ab Shukor, 32; and their son, Muhammad Zafrul Hakimie, 3, who are currently receiving treatment in the Yellow Zone of Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) in Batu Pahat.
The couple’s other son, Muhammad Zariff Hakimie, 2, who sustained severe head injuries, is being treated in the Red Zone of HSNI.
He said the two occupants of the Toyota Vios - its driver, Chin Nyet Boon, 46, and Yong Ah Moi, 81, from Taman Meranti, Bahau, Negeri Sembilan - were also receiving treatment in the Yellow Zone of HSNI for head injuries, while the lorry driver, Mohd Nadzri Abd Wahab, 31, was uninjured.
Recounting the sequence of events, Shahrulanuar said preliminary investigations found that the driver of the southbound Ford Ranger was believed to have lost control of the vehicle while travelling in the left lane along a straight stretch of road before crashing into the rear right side of the lorry, which had stopped on the emergency lane due to engine trouble.
“The impact caused the Ford Ranger to spin before it was hit by the Toyota Vios travelling behind it.
“All the victims’ bodies were taken to the Forensic Medicine Unit of HSNI for post-mortem examinations, and the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Loke announces RM1,000 payout for Melaka taxi drivers ahead of state polls
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke today said taxi drivers in Melaka will receive RM1,000 in assistance on Monday, with the aid funded through proceeds from the sale of special “H” vehicle registration numbers.
Speaking at Pakatan Harapan's (PH) candidate announcement event in Melaka last night, the DAP secretary-general said the assistance formed part of the federal government's efforts to direct public funds towards initiatives that benefit ordinary Malaysians.
“To the taxi drivers in Melaka, I will distribute the RM1,000 to you on Monday,” Loke said, according to the
New Straits Times
(NST).
Loke said the payment would be funded through proceeds from the sale of special “H” vehicle registration numbers, which raised RM91 million.
He said the aid demonstrated how government revenue could be redirected to benefit the public, adding that Putrajaya remained committed to targeted assistance programmes aimed at easing cost-of-living pressures.
Separately, Loke said Pakatan Harapan remained upbeat about its prospects in the Melaka election despite its recent setback in Negri Sembilan.

Title: Singapore consulate in Kuching to be located within Kuching South City Council area, says mayor
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 25 — The much-anticipated Consulate-General of Singapore in Kuching will be located within the Kuching South City Council’s (MBKS) jurisdiction, according to Kuching South Mayor Datuk Wee Hong Seng.
He said the location is likely to be in an area that has recently gained popularity among locals, in the vicinity of high-end residential neighbourhoods.
“More details will soon be publicly announced,” he said during his Facebook live session ‘Shall WEE Talk’ on Saturday.
He made the disclosure in response to netizens’ enquiries about the potential location of the consulate.
Wee went on to provide a few clues on the location, saying it is now a popular area, features high-end residential properties, and that its name contains the word ‘bank’.
However, he did not reveal the precise location.
It is noted that the plan to establish a Consulate-General of Singapore in Kuching was first proposed in 2023.
The proposal was highlighted when Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg attended the 10th Malaysia-Singapore Leaders’ Retreat held in Singapore, where he agreed to the establishment of the consulate.
Abang Johari pointed out that the consulate would help further strengthen bilateral ties and foster cooperation between Sarawak and Singapore in sectors including economy and tourism.
During a courtesy call on Abang Johari in January this year, High Commissioner of Singapore to Malaysia Vanu Gopala Menon announced that Singapore intended to set up consulates in both Kuching and Kota Kinabalu to enhance connections in trade, investment and tourism.
Vanu said the Singaporean Government had approved the plan by November 2023.
Following this approval, Singapore has been identifying suitable premises in Kuching and Kota Kinabalu, including the possible use of temporary office space during the initial phase. — The Borneo Post
